Abstentions; Failures to Vote and Broker Non-Votes An abstention occurs when a Personalis Stockholder returns a proxy with an “abstain” instruction. At the Personalis Special
Meeting, abstentions will be counted as present for purposes of determining whether a quorum exists. An abstention or failure to vote will have the same effect as a vote “AGAINST” the Merger Proposal. An abstention will have
the same effect as a vote “AGAINST” the Merger Compensation Proposal and “AGAINST” the Adjournment Proposal. A failure to vote will have no effect on the vote for the Merger Compensation Proposal and the Adjournment
Proposal . If you sign and return your proxy or voting instruction card without indicating how to vote on any particular proposal, the
shares of Personalis Common Stock represented by your proxy will be voted as recommended by the Personalis Board with respect to that proposal. This means they will be voted: (1) “ FOR ” the Merger Proposal,
(2) “ FOR ” the Merger Compensation Proposal, and (3) “ FOR ” the Adjournment Proposal. Broker non-votes occur when (i) a bank, broker or other nominee has discretionary authority to vote on one or more proposals to be voted on at a meeting of stockholders, but is not permitted to vote on other proposals
without instructions from the beneficial owner of the shares and (ii) the beneficial owner fails to provide the bank, broker or other nominee with such instructions. Under the rules of Nasdaq, your bank, broker or other nominee will only be
permitted to vote your Personalis Common Stock, as applicable, on “non-routine” matters if you instruct your bank, broker or other nominee how to vote. All of the proposals scheduled for
consideration at the Personalis Special Meeting are “non-routine” matters. As a result, if you fail to provide voting instructions to your broker, bank or other nominee, your Personalis Common
Stock will not be counted as present or represented at the Personalis Special Meeting, as applicable, for purposes of determining a quorum and will not be voted on any of the proposals. To make sure that your Personalis Common Stock is voted on each
of the proposals, you should instruct your bank, broker or other nominee how you wish to vote your Personalis Common Stock in accordance with the procedures provided by your bank, broker or other nominee regarding the voting of your Personalis
Common Stock. Broker non-votes will have the same effect as a vote “AGAINST” the Merger Proposal, but will have no effect on the vote for the Merger Compensation Proposal and the Adjournment
Proposal. Virtual attendance at the Personalis Special Meeting constitutes presence in person for purposes of the vote required. Effects of the Mergers; Directors and Officers The Merger Agreement provides for a two-step merger structure. In the First Merger, at the Effective
Time, Merger Sub I will merge with Personalis in accordance with the DGCL, with Personalis surviving the First Merger as a direct, wholly owned subsidiary of Tempus. Immediately following the First Merger, the First Surviving Company will merge with
Merger Sub II in the Second Merger in accordance with the DGCL and the NRS, with Merger Sub II surviving the Second Merger as a direct, wholly owned subsidiary of Tempus. At the Effective Time, the certificate of incorporation and bylaws of Merger Sub I in effect immediately prior to the Effective Time will
become the certificate of incorporation and bylaws of the First Surviving Company. At the Second Effective Time, the articles of organization and operating agreement of Merger Sub II in effect immediately prior to the Second Effective Time will
become the articles of organization and operating agreement of the Surviving Company, except that the articles of organization will be amended to change the Surviving Company’s name to “Personalis, LLC.” Unless Tempus determines
otherwise, the officers and directors of Merger Sub I immediately prior to the Effective Time will become the officers and directors of the First Surviving Company, and the managers and officers of Merger Sub II immediately prior to the Second
Effective Time will become the managers and officers of the Surviving Company. Closing and Effective Time of the Mergers The closing of the First Merger will take place by electronic exchange of deliverables as promptly as practicable, and in any event no later
than 8:00 a.m., New York City time, on the third business day after the satisfaction or, to the extent permitted by applicable law, waiver, of the closing conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement (other than those conditions that by their nature
are to be satisfied at the Closing, but subject to the satisfaction or, to the extent permitted by applicable law, waiver, of such conditions), unless another date, time or place is agreed in writing by Tempus and Personalis. At the Closing, the
parties will cause a certificate of merger 131 Table of Contents with respect to the First Merger to be filed with the Delaware Secretary of State. The First Merger will become effective upon such filing (or such later date and time as specified in the
certificate of merger and agreed by the parties), referred to as the “Effective Time.” Immediately after the First Merger, but in any event on the same day, the parties will cause a certificate of merger with respect to the Second Merger
to be filed with the Delaware Secretary of State and articles of merger to be filed with the Nevada Secretary of State. The Second Merger will become effective upon such filings (or such later date and time as specified therein and agreed by the
parties), such date and time being referred to as the Second Effective Time. Merger Consideration; Proration At the Effective Time, each share of Personalis Common Stock issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time (other than the Cancelled Shares
and the Dissenting Shares) will be converted automatically into the right to receive the following (collectively, the “Merger Consideration”): • the Stock Consideration, consisting of a number of validly issued, fully paid and nonassessable shares of Tempus
Class A Common Stock equal to the “Exchange Ratio,” which will be: (a) 0.3356, if the Tempus Stock Price is equal to or less than the Floor Price of $48.42; or (b) the quotient of $16.25 divided by the Tempus Stock Price, if
the Tempus Stock Price exceeds the Floor Price; • if there is a Tempus Cash Election to pay Cash Consideration for up to 50% of the aggregate number of outstanding
shares of Personalis Common Stock (the number of shares subject to such election, the “Cash Share Number”), an amount equal to the Cash Consideration, consisting of (i) $16.25 per share in cash, without interest (which may include a
fraction of a share and, in that context, will be rounded to the nearest four decimal places), in respect of such holder’s pro rata portion of shares of Personalis Common Stock subject to the Tempus Cash Election with such pro rata percentage
applied identically across all Personalis Stockholders, and (ii) the Stock Consideration for the holder’s remaining shares; • cash in lieu of any fractional shares of Tempus Class A Common Stock, calculated based on the Tempus Stock
Price, without any separately bargained-for consideration; and • such amounts, if any, of post-closing distributions payable in respect of the Tempus Class A Common Stock
issuable in the First Merger. Tempus may make the Tempus Cash Election at any time prior to the third business day
before the Closing Date by providing written notice to Personalis specifying the Cash Share Number and the aggregate amount of cash consideration to be paid. Once given, such notice may not be withdrawn, revoked or otherwise modified without
Personalis’ prior written consent. The Cash Share Number may not exceed 50% of the outstanding shares of Personalis Common Stock (excluding Cancelled Shares). If Tempus makes the Tempus Cash Election, the percentage allocation of the Stock
Consideration and the Cash Consideration will be applied identically across all holders of eligible shares on a pro rata basis. The
Merger Agreement further provides that if the aggregate value of the Stock Consideration payable to Personalis Stockholders (after giving effect to any Tempus Cash Election) would represent less than 40% of the aggregate value of the total
consideration payable in respect of Personalis Common Stock (the “Reorg Threshold”), the Cash Share Number will automatically be reduced to the highest number of shares that would satisfy the Reorg Threshold. This automatic adjustment
mechanism, together with the two-step merger structure, is intended to preserve qualification of the Mergers, taken together, as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the
Code by satisfying the continuity of interest requirement under Treasury Regulations Section 1.368-1(e). Adjustments to Prevent Dilution The
Merger Agreement provides that the Merger Consideration will be adjusted, without duplication, to reflect appropriately the effect of any stock split, reverse stock split, stock dividend (including any dividend or 132 Table of Contents distribution of securities convertible into Personalis Common Stock or Tempus Class A Common Stock), reorganization, recapitalization, reclassification, combination, exchange of shares or
other similar change with respect to the number of outstanding shares of Personalis Common Stock or Tempus Class A Common Stock occurring on or after the date of the Merger Agreement and prior to the Effective Time. This adjustment mechanism is
not intended to permit Personalis or Tempus to take any action with respect to their respective securities that is otherwise prohibited or restricted by the Merger Agreement. Treatment of Personalis Equity Awards Personalis Options Each in-the-money Personalis option that is (a) held by any former employee or non-employee director (whether vested or unvested) or
(b) vested and exercisable and held by any current service provider, in each case that is outstanding and unexercised immediately prior to the Effective Time, will be cancelled in exchange for the Stock Consideration in respect of the net
number of shares of Personalis Common Stock underlying such option immediately prior to the Effective Time (determined after a hypothetical net exercise of the option that gives effect to the exercise price). At the Effective Time, each other in-the-money Personalis option will be assumed and converted into an option to acquire Tempus Class A Common Stock, with the number of shares of Tempus Class A
Common Stock underlying such option and the exercise price thereof adjusted based on the Exchange Ratio, subject to the same terms and conditions applicable to the corresponding Personalis option under the applicable Personalis equity plan and the
agreement evidencing the grant of such option thereunder, including its vesting terms. At the Effective Time, each out-of-the-money Personalis option will be cancelled without consideration. Personalis Restricted Stock Unit Awards At the Effective Time, each Personalis RSU (whether vested or unvested) that is held by a non-employee director will accelerate to become fully vested and be cancelled in exchange for payment of the Stock Consideration in respect of each share of Personalis Common Stock underlying such restricted stock unit award immediately prior to the Effective
Time. At the Effective Time, each other Personalis RSU will be assumed and converted into a Tempus restricted stock unit award, with the number of shares of Tempus Class A Common Stock subject to such award adjusted based on the Exchange Ratio,
subject to the same terms and conditions applicable to the corresponding Personalis RSU under the applicable Personalis Equity Plan and the agreement evidencing the grant of such restricted stock unit award thereunder, including its vesting terms. Personalis Performance Stock Unit Awards At the Effective Time, the unvested portion of each Personalis PSU will vest on a prorated basis based on the portion of the applicable
performance period elapsed as of the closing of the Mergers, with such vested portion of the award cancelled in exchange for payment of the Stock Consideration in respect of each share of Personalis Common Stock underlying such vested portion. At
the Effective Time, each unvested Personalis PSU (after giving effect to the acceleration described in the preceding sentence) will be assumed and converted into a time-based vesting Tempus restricted stock unit award, vesting in equal quarterly
installments over the remainder of the performance measurement period applicable under the award terms, with the number of shares of Tempus Class A Common Stock subject to such award adjusted based on the Exchange Ratio, and will otherwise be
subject to the same terms and conditions applicable to the corresponding original Personalis PSU under the applicable Personalis Equity Plan and the agreement evidencing the grant of such award thereunder (excluding performance-based vesting
conditions). Personalis Employee Stock Purchase Plan Personalis will take all actions with respect to its employee stock purchase plan that are necessary to provide that: (a) with respect to
any offering periods in effect as of the date of the Merger Agreement, no employee who 133 Table of Contents is not a participant in the plan as of the date of the Merger Agreement may become a participant and no participant may increase the percentage amount of his or her payroll deduction election
from that in effect on the date of the Merger Agreement; (b) subject to the consummation of the Mergers, the plan will terminate effective immediately prior to the Effective Time; (c) if the current offering periods terminate prior to the
Effective Time, then the plan will be suspended and no new offering period will be commenced prior to the termination of the Merger Agreement; and (d) if any current offering period is still in effect at the Effective Time, then the last day of
such current offering period will be accelerated to a date within 10 business days prior to the Closing Date, and participants’ accumulated contributions will be used to purchase shares of Personalis Common Stock. Exchange and Payment Procedures Prior to

giving effect to any applicable tax withholding. No interest will accrue or be paid on any Merger Consideration payable upon surrender. Any portion of the Exchange Fund that remains undistributed to Personalis Stockholders for one year after the
Effective Time will, at Tempus’ request, be delivered to Tempus, and former Personalis Stockholders will thereafter be entitled to look only to Tempus (subject to applicable abandoned property, escheat or similar laws) for payment of their

that qualifies as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code, and the Merger Agreement is intended to be, and has been adopted as, a “plan of reorganization” within the meaning of Treasury

that would reasonably be expected to prevent or impede such qualification (and whether the Merger Agreement could, using commercially reasonable efforts, be amended to facilitate such qualification). The parties intend, and, except to the extent
otherwise required by a “determination” within the meaning of Section 1313 of the Code, will report, that the Mergers qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment. In addition, Personalis has agreed to use its reasonable best efforts to deliver a representation letter containing representations of

adverse to Tempus), the Personalis Board Recommendation, (ii) approve, recommend or declare advisable, or publicly propose to approve, recommend or declare advisable, any Acquisition Proposal, (iii) if an Acquisition Proposal has been

(or, if earlier, by the second (2nd) Business Day prior to the Personalis Special Meeting), or (iv) fail to include the Personalis Board Recommendation in this proxy statement/prospectus or the Form S-4 (any action described in this clause (a) being referred to as a Company Adverse Change Recommendation); or (b) approve, recommend or declare advisable, or propose to approve, recommend or declare advisable, or allow Personalis to execute
or enter into any acquisition agreement with respect to an Acquisition Proposal (other than an Acceptable Confidentiality Agreement). Notwithstanding the foregoing, at any time prior to obtaining the Personalis Stockholder Approval, the Personalis Board may make a Company

copies of all transaction documents relating to such Acquisition Proposal), and Personalis has given Tempus five business days (the “Match Period”) after delivery of the Determination Notice to propose revisions to the terms of the
Merger Agreement or make other proposals so that such Acquisition Proposal would cease to constitute a Superior Proposal and has made itself and its representatives reasonably available to negotiate in good faith with Tempus (to the extent Tempus
desires to negotiate) during the Match Period with respect to such proposed revisions or other proposals; and • after considering the terms of the Merger Agreement and any binding written proposals made by Tempus, if any,
prior to 11:59 p.m., Eastern Time on the last day of the Match Period, the Personalis Board has determined, in good faith, that such Acquisition Proposal continues to constitute a Superior Proposal and that the failure to make a Company Adverse
Change Recommendation would be inconsistent with the fiduciary duties of the Personalis Board under applicable law. The
provisions described above also apply to any material amendment, modification or adjustment to any Acquisition Proposal (with any change to the price or form of consideration deemed material) and require a new Determination Notice, except that the
Match Period for such amended proposals will be three business days. In addition, other than in connection with an Acquisition Proposal,
the Personalis Board may make a Company Adverse Change Recommendation in response to a Change in Circumstance (as defined in the Merger Agreement), if and only if: (a) the Personalis Board determines in good faith, after consultation with

constitute the sole and exclusive remedy of Tempus, the Merger Subs and their affiliates against Personalis and its related parties, and receipt of the Reverse Termination Fee will, subject to the same carve-outs, constitute the sole and exclusive
remedy of Personalis and its related parties against Tempus and its affiliates. Each party has acknowledged that the Termination Fee and the Reverse Termination Fee constitute liquidated damages, and not a penalty, reasonably related to the
anticipated harm from termination in the applicable circumstances. Remedies The parties have agreed that irreparable injury, for which monetary damages would not be an adequate remedy, would result if the Merger
Agreement were not performed in accordance with its terms or is otherwise breached, and that each party is entitled to seek an injunction, specific performance or other equitable relief to prevent or remedy any breach or threatened breach, in
addition to any other remedy available at law or in equity, without the need to post any bond or other security. Except as otherwise provided, remedies under the Merger Agreement are cumulative and not exclusive of one another; however, as described
above, a party’s right to receive the Termination Fee or the Reverse Termination Fee, once paid, generally operates as that party’s sole and exclusive remedy in the specified circumstances, and either party may elect either specific
performance to cause the other party to consummate the Closing or receipt of the Termination Fee or the Reverse Termination Fee, as applicable, but not both. Amendment and Waiver The Merger
Agreement may be amended, modified or supplemented only by a written agreement signed by each of Tempus, the Merger Subs and Personalis, subject to applicable law. At any time prior to the Effective Time, Personalis, on the one hand, and Tempus and
the Merger Subs, on the other hand, may extend the time for performance of the other parties’ obligations, waive inaccuracies in the other parties’ representations and warranties, or waive compliance with the other parties’
covenants or conditions for their benefit, in each case only by a written instrument signed by the waiving or extending party. Stock and cash pursuant to the Mergers. This discussion does not address any tax consequences arising under the laws of any state, local or foreign jurisdiction, or under any United States federal laws other than those pertaining to income tax. This
discussion assumes that the Mergers will be completed in accordance with the Merger Agreement and as further described in this proxy statement/prospectus. This discussion is based upon the Code, the regulations promulgated under the Code and court
and administrative rulings and decisions, all as in effect on the date of this proxy statement/prospectus. These laws may change, possibly retroactively, and any change could affect the accuracy of the statements and conclusions set forth in this
discussion. This discussion applies only to U.S. holders and non-U.S. holders that hold their shares of Personalis Common Stock as a capital asset within the meaning of Section 1221 of the Code
(generally, property held for investment). Further, this discussion does not address all aspects of United States federal income taxation that may be relevant to you in light of your particular circumstances or that may be applicable to you if you
are subject to special treatment under the United States federal income tax laws, including if you are: • a financial institution; • a tax-exempt organization; • a pass-through entity (or an investor in a pass-through entity); • an insurance company; • a mutual fund; • a dealer or broker in stocks and securities, or currencies; • a trader in securities that elects mark-to-market treatment; • a holder of Personalis Common Stock acquired through the exercise of an employee stock option, through a tax
qualified retirement plan or otherwise as compensation; • a person that has a functional currency other than the U.S. dollar; • a real estate investment trust; • a regulated investment company; • a controlled foreign corporation, foreign controlled foreign corporation, passive foreign investment company or
corporation that accumulates earnings to avoid U.S. federal income tax; • a person that holds shares of Personalis Common Stock as part of a hedge, straddle, appreciated financial
position, constructive sale, conversion, integrated or other risk reduction transaction; • a person exercising dissenters’ rights; • a U.S. expatriate or former long-term resident; or • a holder that actually or constructively owns (or actually or constructively owned at any time during the
five-year period ending on the date of the disposition of such holder’s Personalis Common Stock pursuant to the Mergers) 5% or more of Personalis Common Stock. In addition, the discussion does not address any alternative minimum tax or any state, local or foreign tax consequences of the Mergers, nor
does it address any tax consequences arising under the unearned income Medicare contribution tax pursuant to the Health Care and Education Reconciliation Act of 2010. Determining the actual tax consequences of the Mergers to you may be complex. They will depend on your specific situation and on factors that
are not within the control of Personalis or Tempus. You should consult with 166 Table of Contents your own tax advisor as to the tax consequences of the Mergers in your particular circumstances. For purposes of this discussion, the term “U.S. holder” means a beneficial owner of
Personalis Common Stock that is for United States federal income tax purposes (a) an individual citizen or resident of the United States, (b) a corporation, or entity treated as a corporation, organized in or under the laws of the United
States or any state thereof or the District of Columbia, (c) a trust if (i) a court within the United States is able to exercise primary supervision over the administration of the trust and one or more “United States persons”
(as defined in the Code) have the authority to control all substantial decisions of the trust or (ii) a valid election is in effect under applicable Treasury Regulations to treat such trust as a United States person, or (d) an estate, the
income of which is includible in gross income for U.S. federal income tax purposes regardless of its source. For purposes of this discussion, the term “non-U.S. holder” means a beneficial owner of
Personalis Common Stock that is neither a U.S. holder nor an entity or arrangement treated as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes. The U.S. federal income tax consequences to a partner in an entity or arrangement that is treated as a
partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes and that holds Personalis Common Stock generally will depend on the status of the partner and the activities of the partnership. Partners in a partnership holding Personalis Common Stock should
consult their own tax advisors. Tax Consequences of the Mergers Generally The Intended Tax Treatment for the First Merger and Second Merger, taken together, is a single integrated transaction that qualifies as a
“reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code, and the Merger Agreement has been adopted as a “plan of reorganization” within the meaning of Treasury Regulations Sections 1.368-2(g) and 1.368-3(a). Receipt of the Personalis Tax Opinion is a condition to Personalis’ obligation to complete the Mergers, which condition
Personalis may waive. Receipt of an analogous tax opinion is not a condition to Tempus’ obligation to complete the Mergers. Each of Cooley LLP, as counsel to Personalis, and Latham & Watkins LLP, as counsel to Tempus, has delivered an
opinion, filed as an exhibit to the registration statement of which this proxy statement/prospectus forms a part, to the effect that, subject to the exceptions, assumptions and qualifications described therein, the Mergers will qualify for the
Intended Tax Treatment (such tax opinions, the “S-4 Tax Opinions”). Each of the Personalis Tax Opinion and the S-4 Tax Opinions is based on representations
made by Tempus and Personalis in tax representation letters and on certain assumptions, all of which must be accurate and complete as of the time each such opinion is delivered. Tempus and Personalis have not sought and will not seek any ruling from the IRS regarding any matters relating to the Mergers, and an opinion
of counsel represents counsel’s best legal judgment and is not binding on the IRS or the courts. Accordingly, no assurance can be given that the IRS will not assert, or that a court would not sustain, a position contrary to any of the
conclusions set forth below. If the Mergers are determined not to qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment, a holder of Personalis Common Stock generally would recognize taxable gain or loss upon the exchange of Personalis Common Stock for Tempus
Class A Common Stock and cash pursuant to the Mergers. See “—Tax Consequences if the Mergers Do Not Qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment ” below. U.S. Holders Exchange for Tempus Class A
Common Stock and Cash • A U.S. holder who receives shares of Tempus Class A Common Stock and cash (other than cash received in lieu
of a fractional share) in exchange for shares of Personalis Common Stock generally will recognize gain (but not loss) in an amount equal to the lesser of (a) the amount of gain realized (i.e., the excess of the sum of the amount of cash and the
fair market value of the Tempus Class A Common Stock received pursuant to the Mergers over such U.S. holder’s adjusted tax basis in the shares of Personalis Common Stock surrendered) and (b) the amount of cash received pursuant to
the Mergers (excluding any cash received in lieu of a fractional share). • If you acquired different blocks of Personalis Common Stock at different times or different prices, you should
consult your tax advisor regarding the manner in which gain or loss should be determined. Any 167 Table of Contents recognized gain generally will be long-term capital gain if, as of the Effective Time, your holding period with respect to the Personalis Common Stock
surrendered exceeds one year. Notwithstanding the foregoing, under Section 356(a)(2) of the Code, all or a portion of the gain recognized by a U.S. holder may be treated as dividend income if the receipt of cash in the Mergers has the effect of
a distribution of a dividend. This determination generally is made under the principles of Sections 302 and 318 of the Code by treating the U.S. holder as if it first received solely Tempus Class A Common Stock in the Mergers and Tempus then
redeemed a portion of that stock for the cash actually received in the Mergers, taking into account all Tempus stock actually or constructively owned by the U.S. holder. Any amount treated as a dividend generally would be limited to the U.S.
holder’s ratable share of the applicable undistributed earnings and profits, and any remaining recognized gain generally would be treated as gain from the exchange of property. A U.S. holder with a relatively minimal actual and constructive
interest in Personalis and Tempus that experiences a meaningful reduction in its proportionate interest in Tempus generally should not be treated as receiving a dividend. Because this determination depends on each holder’s particular
circumstances, U.S. holders of Personalis Common Stock, particularly holders that actually or constructively own Tempus stock other than stock received in the Mergers, should consult their tax advisors. • The aggregate tax basis in the shares of Tempus Class A Common Stock that you receive pursuant to the
Mergers, including any fractional share interests deemed received and redeemed as described below, will equal your aggregate adjusted tax basis in the Personalis Common Stock you surrender, reduced by the amount of cash received (excluding any cash
received in lieu of a fractional share) and increased by the amount of gain, if any, recognized by you (excluding any gain recognized with respect to cash received in lieu of a fractional share) on the exchange. Exchange Solely for Tempus Class A Common Stock • A U.S. holder who receives solely shares of Tempus Class A Common Stock in exchange for shares of Personalis
Common Stock generally will not recognize any gain or loss upon the Mergers. The aggregate tax basis of the Tempus Class A Common Stock received pursuant to the Mergers will be equal to such U.S. holder’s aggregate adjusted tax basis in
the shares of Personalis Common Stock surrendered. The holding period of the Tempus Class A Common Stock received pursuant to the Mergers (including any fractional share deemed received and redeemed as described below) will include such U.S.
holder’s holding period of the Personalis Common Stock surrendered. Cash in Lieu of a Fractional Share A U.S. holder of Personalis Common Stock who receives cash in lieu of a fractional share of Tempus Class A Common Stock will be treated as
having received the fractional share of Tempus Class A Common Stock pursuant to the Mergers and then as having sold that fractional share for cash. As a result, such U.S. holder generally will recognize gain or loss equal to the difference
between the amount of cash received and the portion of such U.S. holder’s adjusted tax basis in the Personalis Common Stock surrendered that is allocable to such fractional share. This gain or loss generally will be capital gain or loss, and
will be long-term capital gain or loss if, as of the Effective Time, such U.S. holder’s holding period for the Personalis Common Stock surrendered is greater than one year. The deductibility of capital
losses is subject to limitations. Tax Consequences if the Mergers Do Not Qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment If the Mergers, taken together, do not qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment, a U.S. holder of Personalis Common Stock generally would
recognize capital gain or loss for U.S. federal income tax purposes on each share of Personalis Common Stock surrendered in the Mergers in an amount equal to the difference between (a) the sum of the fair market value, as of the Effective Time,
of the Tempus Class A Common Stock and the amount of any cash received pursuant to the Mergers (including any cash received in lieu of a fractional share) in exchange 168 Table of Contents for such share and (b) such U.S. holder’s adjusted tax basis in such share. If a U.S. holder acquired different blocks of shares of Personalis Common Stock at different times or
different prices, gain or loss must be calculated separately for each block of Personalis Common Stock exchanged by such U.S. holder. Any such gain or loss would be long-term capital gain or loss if the U.S.
holder’s holding period in a particular block of Personalis Common Stock exceeds one year at the Effective Time. Under current law, long-term capital gain of non-corporate U.S. holders (including individuals) generally is taxed at reduced U.S. federal income tax rates. The deductibility of capital losses is subject to limitations. A U.S. holder’s aggregate
tax basis in shares of Tempus Class A Common Stock received in the Mergers would be equal to the fair market value thereof as of the Effective Time, and such U.S. holder’s holding period in such shares would begin on the day after the
Effective Time. Non-U.S. Holders Non-U.S. holders generally will recognize gain or loss (as applicable) on the same basis as U.S.
holders, as described above under “—U.S. Holders .” However, subject to the discussion below under “ —Backup Withholding and Information Reporting ” and “ —FATCA ,” a non-U.S. holder generally will not be subject to U.S. federal income tax on any gain recognized on the exchange of Personalis Common Stock for Tempus Class A Common Stock and cash pursuant to the Mergers,
unless: • the gain is effectively connected with the conduct by such non-U.S. holder of a trade or business within the United States (and, if an applicable income tax treaty so requires, is attributable to a permanent establishment maintained by such non-U.S. holder in the United
States), in which case the non-U.S. holder generally will be subject to U.S. federal income tax on such gain in the same manner as a U.S. holder, and a non-U.S. holder
that is a corporation may also be subject to a branch profits tax at a rate of 30% (or such lower rate as may be specified by an applicable income tax treaty); • such non-U.S. holder is an individual who is present in the United States
for 183 days or more in the taxable year of the Mergers and certain other conditions are met, in which case the non-U.S. holder generally will be subject to U.S. federal income tax at a rate of 30% (or such
lower rate as may be specified by an applicable income tax treaty) on the amount by which such holder’s capital gains allocable to U.S. sources exceed capital losses allocable to U.S. sources; or • Personalis is or has been a “United States real property holding corporation” within the meaning of
Section 897(c)(2) of the Code at any time during the applicable period specified in Section 897(c)(1)(A)(ii) of the Code. Personalis has represented in the Merger Agreement that it has not been a United States real property holding
corporation during such period, and Personalis is required to deliver to Tempus prior to the closing of the Mergers a certification to the effect that the shares of Personalis Common Stock are not United States real property interests as defined in
Section 897(c) of the Code, together with a notice to the IRS, in accordance with Treasury Regulations under Sections 897 and 1445 of the Code. In addition, in the limited circumstances in which a non-U.S. holder’s recognized gain is
treated as having the effect of a distribution of a dividend under the principles of Sections 302 and 318 of the Code, as described above under “ —U.S. Holders—Exchange for Tempus Class A Common Stock and
Cash ,” the amount so treated generally would be subject to U.S. federal withholding tax at a rate of 30%, unless reduced or eliminated by an applicable income tax treaty. Because the possibility of dividend treatment depends upon each
holder’s particular circumstances, including the application of constructive ownership rules, non-U.S. holders should consult their tax advisors regarding the application of the foregoing rules to their
particular circumstances, including the availability of, and procedures for claiming, any treaty benefits. 169 Table of Contents Backup Withholding and Information Reporting Payments of cash to a non-corporate U.S. holder of Personalis Common Stock in connection with the
Mergers may be subject to information reporting and backup withholding (currently at a rate of twenty-four percent (24%)). Such a U.S. holder generally will not be subject to backup withholding, however, if
the holder: • furnishes a correct taxpayer identification number, certifies that such holder is not subject to backup
withholding on IRS form W-9 (or an applicable substitute or successor form) included in the letter of transmittal such holder will receive and otherwise complies with all the applicable requirements of the
backup withholding rules; or • provides proof of an applicable exemption from backup withholding. A non-U.S. holder may be required to establish an exemption from information reporting and backup
withholding with respect to any cash received pursuant to the Mergers by certifying such holder’s non-U.S. status, generally on the appropriate series of IRS Form W-8, or by otherwise establishing an exemption. Any amounts withheld under the backup withholding
rules are not an additional tax and generally will be allowed as a refund or credit against the holder’s United States federal income tax liability, provided the required information is timely furnished to the IRS. FATCA Sections 1471 through 1474
of the Code, together with the Treasury Regulations and administrative guidance issued thereunder (commonly referred to as “FATCA”), generally impose a 30% withholding tax on dividends paid to a foreign financial institution or a non-financial foreign entity unless specified certification, information reporting and other requirements are satisfied. While withholding under FATCA would also have applied to payments of gross proceeds from the
sale or other disposition of stock, proposed Treasury Regulations eliminate FATCA withholding on payments of gross proceeds entirely. Taxpayers generally may rely on these proposed Treasury Regulations until final Treasury Regulations are issued. Non-U.S. holders should consult their tax advisors regarding the potential application of withholding under FATCA in connection with the Mergers. Size of Board of Directors Size of Board of Directors The Tempus Charter provides that the number of directors constituting the Tempus Board is fixed exclusively by resolution of the Tempus
Board. Neither the Tempus Charter nor the Tempus Bylaws establishes a minimum or maximum number of directors. The NRS requires every Nevada corporation to have at least one director. Until the Final Conversion Date (as defined in the Tempus Charter), the number of
directors may also be fixed by the affirmative vote of the holders of a majority of the voting power of Tempus Class A Common Stock and Tempus Class B Common Stock, voting together as a single class. The Personalis Charter provides that the management of the business and the conduct of the affairs of Personalis are vested in the Personalis Board, and that the number of directors constituting the Personalis Board is fixed
exclusively by resolutions adopted by a majority of the authorized number of directors constituting the Personalis Board. The Personalis Charter does not provide for the number of directors to be fixed by stockholder vote, and neither the Personalis
Charter nor the Personalis Bylaws establishes a minimum or maximum number of directors. 173 Table of Contents Tempus Personalis Election of Directors Election of Directors Directors are elected at each annual meeting of Tempus Stockholders by a plurality of the votes of the shares present in person, by remote communication or represented by proxy and entitled to vote on the election of directors, and
each director serves until his or her successor is elected and qualified or until his or her earlier death, resignation or removal. The Personalis Board is divided into three classes. The directors in each class serve for a three-year term, with one class being elected
each year by the Personalis Stockholders at the annual meeting of the Personalis Stockholders. Each Personalis director serves until his or her successor is duly elected and qualified or until his or her earlier death, resignation or removal. Personalis
directors are elected by a plurality of the votes cast. Removal of Directors Removal of Directors Any individual director or the entire Tempus Board may be removed as provided in NRS 78.335, which requires the vote of stockholders representing not less than two-thirds of the voting power
of the issued and outstanding stock entitled to vote. Neither the Tempus Charter nor the Tempus Bylaws requires that removal be “for cause.” The Personalis Charter provides that no member of the Personalis Board may be removed from office by the Personalis Stockholders except for cause and, in addition to any other vote required by law, upon the approval of not less than two-thirds of the total voting power of all of Personalis’ outstanding voting stock then entitled to vote in the election of directors. Vacancies of the Board of Directors Vacancies of the Board of Directors Subject to the rights of the holders of any series of preferred stock, vacancies on the Tempus Board and newly created directorships may be
filled by the affirmative vote of a majority of the directors then in office, even if less than a quorum, or by the sole remaining director. If the vacancy is created prior to the Final Conversion Date, it may also be filled by the holders of a majority of the voting power of the outstanding Tempus
Class A Common Stock and Tempus Class B Common Stock, voting together as a single class. Any director so elected holds office for the remainder of the full term of the vacant directorship. Subject to any limitations imposed by applicable law and subject to the rights of the holders of any series of Preferred Stock, any vacancies
on the Personalis Board resulting from death, resignation, disqualification, removal or other causes and any newly created directorships resulting from any increase in the number of directors, shall, unless the Personalis Board determines by
resolution that any such vacancies or newly created directorships shall be filled by the stockholders and except as otherwise provided by applicable law, be filled only by the affirmative vote of a majority of the directors then in office, even
though less than a quorum of the Personalis Board. Any director elected shall hold
office for the remainder of the full term of the director for which the vacancy was created or occurred and until such director’s successor shall have been elected and qualified. Requirements for Advance Notification of Stockholder Proposals Requirements for Advance Notification of Stockholder Proposals A Tempus Stockholder seeking to nominate a director or bring other business before an annual meeting must be a stockholder of record entitled
to vote at the meeting, deliver timely written notice to Tempus’ Secretary and comply with the notice procedures in the Tempus Bylaws. To be timely, notice must be received not earlier than 120 days nor later than 90 days prior to the first anniversary of the preceding year’s annual
meeting; provided, however, that if the meeting is advanced more than 30 days prior to, or delayed more than 70 days after, such anniversary, notice must be received not earlier than 120 days prior to the meeting and not later than the later of 90
days prior to the meeting or the tenth day following public announcement of the meeting date. With respect to nominations at a special meeting at which directors are to be elected, notice must be received not earlier than 120 days prior to the
meeting and not later than the later of 90 days prior to the meeting or the tenth day following public announcement of the meeting date and the Tempus Board’s nominees. entitled to vote and comply with the advance notice and disclosure requirements in the Personalis Charter and the Personalis Bylaws. To be timely, a stockholder’s notice must be received not later than the close of business on the 90th day, nor earlier than the close of business on the
120th day, prior to the first anniversary of the preceding year’s annual meeting; if no annual meeting was held in the preceding year, or the meeting date is moved more than 30 days before or after that anniversary, notice must be received not
earlier than 120 days before the meeting and not later than the later of 90 days before the meeting or the 10th day following public announcement of the meeting date. ownership, derivative positions, independence 175 Table of Contents Tempus Personalis questionnaires, and representations regarding voting commitments and compliance with governance policies. Indemnification of Directors and Officers Indemnification of Directors and Officers The Tempus Bylaws provide that Tempus will indemnify, to the fullest extent permitted under the NRS or other applicable law, any person who
is or is threatened to be made a party to, or is otherwise involved in, any threatened, pending or completed proceeding by reason of the fact that such person is or was a director or executive officer of Tempus, or was serving at Tempus’
request as a director, officer, employee or agent of another enterprise, against expenses, judgments, fines and amounts paid in settlement. Tempus is not required to indemnify a director or executive officer in connection with a proceeding initiated
by that person, subject to limited exceptions, and has the power to indemnify its other officers, employees and agents. Tempus will advance expenses to any director or executive officer prior to the final disposition of a proceeding, subject, if required by the NRS, to delivery
of an undertaking to repay amounts advanced if it is ultimately determined that the person is not entitled to indemnification. These rights are contractual rights that vest when the person becomes a director or executive officer, continue after
service ends and are not exclusive of other rights, and Tempus is authorized to enter into individual indemnification agreements and to purchase and maintain directors’ and officers’ liability insurance. The Personalis Charter provides that, to the fullest extent under applicable law, Personalis shall indemnify and hold harmless against all
liability and loss suffered and expenses (including attorneys’ fees) reasonably incurred by a person, if such person was or is made or is threatened to be made a party or is otherwise involved in any proceeding by reason of the fact that he or
she is or was a director or executive officer of Personalis, or, while such person is or was serving as a director or executive officer of Personalis, or while such person is or was serving at the request of Personalis as a director, officer,
employee or agent of another corporation or of a partnership, joint venture, trust, enterprise or nonprofit entity, including service with respect to employee benefit plans. Personalis is not required to indemnify any director or officer in
connection with any proceeding (or part thereof) initiated by such person unless (i) such indemnification is expressly required to be made by applicable law, (ii) the proceeding was authorized by the Personalis Board, (iii) such
indemnification is provided by Personalis, in its sole discretion, pursuant to the powers vested in Personalis under applicable law or (iv) such indemnification is otherwise required to be made under the Personalis Charter. The Personalis Charter further provides that Personalis may provide additional
indemnification by individual contracts with its directors and executive officers. With certain exceptions, the indemnification agreements with Personalis’ directors and officers provide for indemnification for related expenses, including
attorneys’ fees, judgments, fines, and settlement amounts incurred by any of these individuals in connection with any action, proceeding, or investigation. corporation’s total assets would not be less than the sum of its total liabilities plus the amount that would be needed, if the corporation were to be dissolved immediately after the time of the distribution, to satisfy the preferential rights
upon such dissolution of holders of shares of any class or series of the capital stock of the Subject to applicable law and the preferences that may be applicable to any then-outstanding Personalis preferred stock, holders of Personalis Common Stock are entitled to receive ratably those dividends, if any, as may be declared

Business Combinations with Interested Parties Business Combinations with Interested Parties The Tempus Charter expressly opts out of NRS 78.411 to 78.444, Nevada’s combinations with interested stockholders statute, at any time
Tempus is a “resident domestic corporation” as defined in NRS 78.427. The Tempus Bylaws similarly provide, in accordance with NRS 78.378, that NRS 78.378 to 78.3793, relating to acquisitions of controlling interests, do not apply
to Tempus or to any acquisition of Tempus’ capital stock. Neither the Tempus
Charter nor the Tempus Bylaws imposes any supermajority vote, fair price or other special approval requirement on business combinations with interested stockholders. Personalis is subject to Section 203 of the DGCL, which prohibits persons deemed to be “interested stockholders” from engaging in a “business combination” with a publicly held Delaware corporation for
three years following the date these persons become interested stockholders unless the business combination is, or the transaction in which the person became an interested stockholder was, approved in a prescribed manner or another prescribed
exception applies. Generally, an “interested stockholder” is a person who, together with affiliates and associates, owns, or within three years prior to the determination of interested stockholder status did own, 15% or more of a
corporation’s voting stock. Generally, a “business combination” includes a merger, asset or stock sale, or other transaction resulting in a financial benefit to the interested stockholder. 179 Table of Contents PROPOSAL 1—THE MERGER PROPOSAL This proxy statement/prospectus is being furnished to Personalis Stockholders as part of the solicitation of proxies by the Personalis Board

DISCUSSED BELOW. Under Section 262, if the Mergers are completed, holders of record of shares, or beneficial owners, of Personalis
Common Stock who (a) deliver a written demand for appraisal of such person’s shares of Personalis Common Stock to Personalis prior to the vote on the adoption of the Merger Agreement; (b) do not vote, by remote communication or by
proxy, in favor of the adoption of the Merger Agreement; (c) continuously hold of record or beneficially own such shares of Personalis Common Stock on the date of making the demand for appraisal through the Effective Time; (d) otherwise
comply with the procedures and satisfy certain ownership thresholds, as applicable, set forth in Section 262; and (e) do not withdraw such person’s demand or otherwise lose such person’s right to appraisal, may be entitled to
have their shares of Personalis Common Stock appraised by the Delaware Court of Chancery and to receive payment in cash, in lieu of the consideration set forth in the Merger Agreement, for the “fair value” of their shares of Personalis
Common Stock, exclusive of any element of value arising from the accomplishment or expectation of the Mergers, together with (unless the Delaware Court of Chancery in its discretion determines otherwise for good cause shown or as otherwise provided
in Section 262) interest, if any, on the amount determined by the Delaware Court of Chancery to be the fair value from the Effective Time through the date of payment of the judgment (or in certain circumstances described herein, on the
difference between the amount determined to be the fair value and the amount paid by the surviving corporation in the Mergers to each person entitled to appraisal prior to the entry of judgment in the appraisal proceeding) as described further
below. However, after an appraisal petition has been filed, the Delaware Court of Chancery, at a hearing to determine persons entitled to appraisal rights, will dismiss appraisal proceedings as to all holders of shares of a class or series of stock
that, immediately prior to the closing of the Mergers, were listed on a national securities exchange who are otherwise entitled to appraisal rights unless (i) the total number of shares of such class or series of stock for which appraisal
rights have been pursued or perfected exceeds one percent of the outstanding shares of such class or series as measured in accordance with subsection (g) of Section 262 or (ii) the value of the aggregate per share price provided as
consideration in the Mergers in respect of such shares exceeds $1 million (the conditions in the foregoing clauses (i) and (ii), the “Ownership Thresholds”). Given that the shares of Personalis Common Stock are listed on Nasdaq
(and assuming such shares remain so listed up until the closing of the Mergers), then the Delaware Court of Chancery will dismiss any appraisal proceedings as to all holders of Personalis Common Stock who are otherwise entitled to appraisal rights
unless one of the Ownership Thresholds is satisfied with respect to such shares of Personalis Common Stock. 183 Table of Contents Unless the Delaware Court of Chancery, in its discretion, determines otherwise for good
cause shown or as otherwise provided in Section 262, interest, if any, on the amount determined to be the fair value of the shares of Personalis Common Stock subject to appraisal will accrue and compound quarterly from the Effective Time
through the date the judgment is paid at five percent over the Federal Reserve discount rate (including any surcharge) as established from time to time during such period (except that, if at any time before the entry of judgment in the proceeding,
the surviving corporation makes a voluntary cash payment to each person entitled to appraisal, interest will accrue thereafter only upon the sum of (a) the difference, if any, between the amount so paid and the fair value of the shares of
Personalis Common Stock as determined by the Delaware Court of Chancery and (b) interest accrued, unless paid at that time). The Surviving Entity is under no obligation to make such voluntary cash payment prior to such entry of judgment. prescribed in Section 262. The failure to file such a petition within the period specified in Section 262 could nullify a previous written demand for appraisal. Within 120 days after the effective date of the Mergers, any person who has complied with the requirements for an appraisal of such
person’s shares of Personalis Common Stock pursuant to Section 262 will be entitled, upon written request, to receive from the Surviving Entity a statement setting forth the aggregate number of shares of Personalis Common Stock not voted
in favor of the adoption of the Merger Agreement and with respect to which Personalis has received demands for appraisal, and the aggregate number of stockholders or beneficial owners holding or owning such shares ( provided that, where a
beneficial owner makes a demand for appraisal directly, the record holder of such shares shall not be considered a separate stockholder holding such shares for purposes of this aggregate number). Such statement must be given within 10 days after
receipt by the Surviving Entity of the written request for such a statement or within 10 days after the expiration of the period for delivery of demands for appraisal, whichever is later. If a petition for an appraisal is duly filed by any person other than the Surviving Entity, service of a copy thereof must be made upon the
Surviving Entity, which will then be obligated within 20 days after such service to file with the Delaware Register in Chancery a duly verified list (which we refer to as the “verified list”) containing the names and addresses of all
persons who have demanded appraisal for their shares of Personalis Common Stock and with whom agreements as to the value of their shares of Personalis Common Stock have not been reached. The Delaware Court of Chancery may order the Register in
Chancery to give notice of the time and place fixed for the hearing of such petition to the surviving corporation and all of the persons shown on the verified list at the addresses stated therein. The costs of any such notice are borne by the
Surviving Entity. After notice is provided to the applicable persons as required by the Delaware Court of Chancery, at the hearing on
such petition, the Delaware Court of Chancery will determine the persons who have complied with Section 262 and who have become entitled to appraisal rights thereunder. The Delaware Court of Chancery may require the persons who demanded
appraisal for their shares of Personalis Common Stock and who hold Personalis Common Stock represented by stock certificates to submit their stock certificates to the Register in 186 Table of Contents Chancery for notation thereon of the pendency of the appraisal proceedings. Accordingly, persons holding stock represented by stock certificates and wishing to seek appraisal of their shares of
Personalis Common Stock are cautioned to retain their stock certificates pending resolution of the appraisal proceedings. If any person fails to comply with this requirement, the Delaware Court of Chancery may dismiss the proceedings as to such
person. Upon application by the Surviving Entity or by any person entitled to participate in the appraisal proceeding, the Delaware Court of Chancery may, in its discretion, proceed to trial upon the appraisal prior to the final determination of the
persons entitled to an appraisal. Any person whose name appears on the verified list may participate fully in all proceedings until it is finally determined that such person is not entitled to appraisal rights under Section 262. Given that the shares of Personalis Common Stock are listed on Nasdaq (and assuming such shares remain so listed up until closing of the
Mergers), the Delaware Court of Chancery will dismiss any appraisal proceedings as to all holders of shares of Personalis Common Stock who are otherwise entitled to appraisal rights unless one of the Ownership Thresholds is met with respect to such
shares of Personalis Common Stock. Determination of Fair Value After the Delaware Court of Chancery determines the persons entitled to appraisal and, with respect to Personalis Common Stock, that at least
one of the Ownership Thresholds above has been satisfied in respect of persons seeking appraisal rights, then the appraisal proceeding will be conducted in accordance with the rules of the Delaware Court of Chancery, including any rules specifically
governing appraisal proceedings. Through such proceeding, the Delaware Court of Chancery will determine the “fair value” of the shares of Personalis Common Stock, exclusive of any element of value arising from the accomplishment or
expectation of the Mergers, together with interest, if any, to be paid upon the amount determined to be the fair value. Unless the Delaware Court of Chancery in its discretion determines otherwise for good cause shown or as otherwise provided in
Section 262, interest from the Effective Time through the date of payment of the judgment will be compounded quarterly and will accrue at five percent over the Federal Reserve discount rate (including any surcharge) as established from time to
time during the period between the Effective Time and the date of payment of the judgment. However, the Surviving Entity has the right, at any time prior to the Delaware Court of Chancery’s entry of judgment in the proceedings, to make a
voluntary cash payment to each person seeking appraisal. If the Surviving Entity makes a voluntary cash payment pursuant to subsection (h) of Section 262, interest will accrue thereafter only on the sum of (a) the difference, if any,
between the amount paid by the surviving corporation in such voluntary cash payment and the fair value of the shares of Personalis Common Stock as determined by the Delaware Court of Chancery and (b) interest accrued before such voluntary cash
payment, unless paid at that time. In determining fair value, the Delaware Court of Chancery will take into account all relevant factors.
In Weinberger v. UOP, Inc. , the Delaware Supreme Court discussed the factors that could be considered in determining fair value in an appraisal proceeding, stating that “proof of value by any techniques or methods which are
generally considered acceptable in the financial community and otherwise admissible in court” should be considered, and that “[f]air price obviously requires consideration of all relevant factors involving the value of a company.”
The Delaware Supreme Court stated that, in making this determination of fair value, the court must consider market value, asset value, dividends, earnings, prospects, the nature of the enterprise and any other facts that could be ascertained as of
the date of the merger that “throw any light on future prospects of the merged corporation.” Section 262 provides that fair value is to be “exclusive of any element of value arising from the accomplishment or expectation of
the merger.” In Cede & Co . v. Technicolor, Inc ., the Delaware Supreme Court stated that such exclusion is a “narrow exclusion [that] does not encompass known elements of value,” but which rather
applies only to the speculative elements of value arising from such accomplishment or expectation. In Weinberger , the Supreme Court of Delaware also stated that “elements of future value, including the nature of the enterprise, which
are known or susceptible of proof as of the date of the merger and not the product of speculation, may be considered.” Persons
considering seeking appraisal should be aware that the fair value of their shares of Personalis Common Stock as so determined by the Delaware Court of Chancery could be more than, the same as or less than the 187 Table of Contents consideration they would receive pursuant to the Mergers if they did not seek appraisal of their shares of Personalis Common Stock and that an opinion of an investment banking firm as to the
fairness, from a financial point of view, of the consideration payable in a merger is not an opinion as to, and does not in any manner address, fair value under Section 262. ALTHOUGH PERSONALIS BELIEVES THAT THE PER SHARE MERGER
CONSIDERATION IS FAIR, NO REPRESENTATION IS MADE AS TO THE OUTCOME OF THE APPRAISAL OF FAIR VALUE AS DETERMINED BY THE DELAWARE COURT OF CHANCERY, AND STOCKHOLDERS AND BENEFICIAL OWNERS SHOULD RECOGNIZE THAT SUCH AN APPRAISAL COULD RESULT IN
A DETERMINATION OF A VALUE HIGHER OR LOWER THAN, OR THE SAME AS, THE PER SHARE MERGER CONSIDERATION. Neither Personalis nor Tempus anticipates offering more than the per share Merger Consideration to any persons exercising appraisal rights, and
each of Personalis and Tempus reserves the right to make a voluntary cash payment pursuant to subsection (h) of Section 262 and to assert, in any appraisal proceeding, that for purposes of Section 262, the “fair value” of
a share of Personalis Common Stock is less than the per share price. If a petition for appraisal is not timely filed or, with respect to Personalis Common Stock, if neither of the ownership thresholds above has been satisfied in respect of persons
seeking appraisal rights, then the right to an appraisal will cease. The Delaware Court of Chancery will direct the payment of the fair
value of the shares of Personalis Common Stock, together with interest, if any, by the surviving corporation to the persons entitled thereto. Payment will be so made to each such person upon such terms and conditions as the Delaware Court of
Chancery may order. The Delaware Court of Chancery’s decree may be enforced as other decrees in the Delaware Court of Chancery may be enforced. The costs of the appraisal proceedings (which do not include attorneys’ fees or the fees and expenses of experts) may be determined by
the Delaware Court of Chancery and taxed upon the parties as the Delaware Court of Chancery deems equitable under the circumstances. Upon application of a person whose name appears on the verified list who participated in the proceeding and incurred
expenses in connection therewith (which we refer to as an “application”), the Delaware Court of Chancery may also order that all or a portion of such expenses, including, without limitation, reasonable attorney’s fees and the fees
and expenses of experts, be charged pro rata against the value of all the shares of Personalis Common Stock entitled to an appraisal that were not dismissed pursuant to the terms of Section 262 or subject to an award pursuant to a reservation.
In the absence of such determination or assessment, each party bears its own expenses. If any person who demands appraisal of shares of
Personalis Common Stock under Section 262 fails to perfect, or loses or validly withdraws, such person’s right to appraisal, such person’s shares of Personalis Common Stock will be deemed to have been converted at the Effective Time
into the right to receive the per share Merger Consideration as provided in the Merger Agreement. A person will fail to perfect, or effectively lose, such person’s right to appraisal if no petition for appraisal is filed within 120 days after
the Effective Time, if, in the case of Personalis Common Stock, neither of the Ownership Thresholds above has been satisfied in respect of those seeking appraisal rights with respect to the shares of Personalis Common Stock, or if the person
delivers to the surviving corporation a written withdrawal of such person’s demand for appraisal and an acceptance of the per share Merger Consideration as provided in the Merger Agreement in accordance with Section 262. From and after the Effective Time, no person who has demanded appraisal rights in compliance with Section 262 will be entitled to vote
such shares of Personalis Common Stock for any purpose or to receive payment of dividends or other distributions on such shares (except dividends or other distributions payable to stockholders of record at a date which is prior to the Effective
Time). Failure to comply with all of the procedures set forth in Section 262 may result in the loss of appraisal rights. In that
event, you will be entitled to receive the per share price for your dissenting shares in accordance with the Merger Agreement, without interest and less any applicable withholding taxes. Consequently, any person wishing to exercise appraisal rights
is encouraged to consult legal counsel before attempting to exercise those rights. 188 Table of Contents LEGAL MATTERS The validity of the shares of Tempus Class A Common Stock issuable under Nevada law in the First Merger will be passed upon for Tempus by
